title: Housekeeping: restructure experiments, fix biases, add validation metrics
description:
Consolidate the accumulated cleanup work into tracked tasks with dependencies.
These emerged from reviewing the experiment results, data generation code, and
monitoring notebook during the coupled-vs-skeleton ablation experiments.

title: Remove constant guarantee bias in RandomBinaryTree
description:
## Problem
RandomBinaryTree._label_leaves (libs/symbolic/src/symbolic/generation/stages.py:97-99) 
forces at least one constant per tree:

    if not any(is_const):
        is_const[int(self.rng.integers(0, n))] = True

This excludes ~20% of the skeleton space (constant-free expressions like
mul(X0,X1), div(sin(X0), exp(X1))). It also skews the effective constant
probability for trees with few leaves.

## Fix
Remove lines 97-99. With p_constant=0.3, some trees will naturally have no
constants — that is correct behavior.

## Verification
- Run symbolic tests: python -m pytest libs/symbolic/tests/ -x -q
- Generate 1000 samples and verify some have zero constants
close_reason: Completed: removed force-constant block (stages.py:97-99), updated docstring and test assertion. 46.3% of trees now have zero constants as expected with p_constant=0.3. Commit a94984c.

title: Add validation loss logging to trial
description:
## Problem
The trial's _evaluate function computes only generation metrics (val_r2, 
val_valid_rate) during validation. It never computes teacher-forced 
validation loss. Without val_loss/val_ce/val_structure_ce, we cannot detect
overfitting or track convergence quality beyond noisy generation metrics.

## Fix
In _evaluate (or a new function), add a no-grad forward pass on the validation
samples using teacher forcing (same as training), then log:
- val_loss (total)
- val_ce (cross-entropy component)
- val_structure_ce (CE excluding NUM tokens)
- val_mse (numeric head component)

These should be logged every val_every steps alongside the existing metrics.

## Scope
- Modify experiments/ablation/trial.py (and probe/trial.py if still used)
- The val samples already exist in the trial loop
- This is a forward pass with existing model/data, no architecture change
close_reason: Completed: added teacher-forced forward pass in _evaluate that logs val_loss, val_ce, val_structure_ce, val_mse alongside existing generation metrics. Commit 22f4c4f.

title: Restructure experiment directories
description:
## Problem
The experiments/ directory has dozens of folders each holding one config.py,
plus symlinks (coupled/trial.py → ../ablation/trial.py). This grew from the
mistaken assumption that trial files must be named trial.py and live in the
same dir as config.py. Jernerics takes trial_file and config_file as separate
path arguments — naming is free.

## Target structure
experiments/
  ablation/trial.py          # shared training + eval loop
  configs/
    coupled.py               # was: experiments/coupled/config.py
    skeleton.py              # was: experiments/skeleton/config.py
    canon_large.py           # was: experiments/canon_large/config.py
    raw_large.py             # was: experiments/raw_large/config.py
    canon_m5.py              # etc.
    canon_m7.py
    raw_m5.py
    raw_m7.py
    pool_canon.py
    pool_raw.py
    easy.py
    diagnostic.py

## Dispatch
jernerics run -b hpc experiments/ablation/trial.py experiments/configs/coupled.py

## Rules
- Consolidate duplicate trial files (diagnostic, overfit, scale, train) into
  the one shared ablation/trial.py
- Delete experiment dirs that only held a config.py
- Delete experiment dirs that only held a trial.py symlink
- Keep experiments/probe/ as a reference (has the most complete trial code)
- Keep experiments/canon/ (has pool generation scripts)
- Keep experiments/timing/ (standalone scripts, not trials)
close_reason: Completed: consolidated 14 config files into experiments/configs/, deleted duplicate trial files and empty experiment dirs, deleted poisoned lambda-sweep configs. Commit 1b5fcdb (amended). Verified all configs load with correct tags and pool paths.

title: Re-run coupled vs skeleton with all fixes
description:
## Dependencies
- symlab-75p.1 (constant guarantee removed)
- symlab-75p.2 (validation loss logging)
- symlab-75p.3 (experiment restructure)

## Purpose
After the housekeeping fixes, re-run the coupled-vs-skeleton ablation with:
- Unbiased data generation (no forced constants)
- Validation loss tracking
- Clean experiment structure
- Log-scale constant normalization (already done, commit ac6c5d6)
- Stats fed directly to numeric head (already done, commit 542f322)
- torch cu128 for cluster compatibility (already done)

This is the definitive test of whether meaningful constant prediction
improves structure representations. Previous runs were contaminated by
the constant guarantee bias and lacked validation metrics.
close_reason: Completed: coupled (26998450) and skeleton (26998456) ran on priority-gpu with unbiased pool (36.3% zero-constant), val loss logging, stats→numhead, log-scale constants. Results show dramatically different pattern from biased pool — func_equiv raw up significantly, func_equiv_fit dropped from ~65% to ~27%. Needs analysis.

title: Remove _SafeSimplify or formalize approach
description:
## Status
Deferred. _SafeSimplify is an experiment-level workaround in probe/trial.py
that wraps sympy.simplify and returns None if it introduces out-of-opset
operators. It works but is not clean.

## Options
1. Keep as experiment-level helper (status quo)
2. Move to library with proper opset-aware simplification
3. Remove canonicalization from the pipeline entirely

Decision deferred — depends on whether canonicalization is still needed
after the other fixes land.

title: Improve training monitor notebook
description:

- Per-step vs per-val-step distinction
- Maybe func_equiv_fit over training (if logged)

## Deferred
Iterative improvement as needed during experiment runs.

title: Rename test_model.py to fix pytest collection clash
description: test_model.py exists in both libs/symbolic/tests/ and models/manifest/tests/. Running pytest from repo root causes import conflicts because both modules have the same basename. Fix: rename one to a unique name (e.g. test_symbolic_model.py / test_manifest_model.py). Trivial but real annoyance every time tests are run.
